On released skgo v0.16.3 (`7803f6439ad4200c560f8482501f5a19467e51d3`), ordinary Go page-load failures during `just dev` return HTTP 500 with `Internal Error`, without the authored error message or user source frame. This was reproduced through the Go development origin with Kit 3 and VitePlus 1.0.0. The server continues serving a healthy route afterward. Reproduction: 1. Create a minimal TypeScript application with the released CLI: `skgo new --origin http://localhost:8080 --skgo-version v0.16.3 --module example.invalid/devdiagnostics devdiagnostics -- --template minimal --types ts --add vitest=usages:unit`. 2. Add `web/src/routes/error/page.server.go`: ```go package errorproof import ( "context" "errors" "github.com/tylergannon/skgo" ) type PageData struct { Receipt string `json:"receipt"` } func errorLoad(ctx context.Context) (PageData, error) { return PageData{}, errors.New("DEV_DIAG_SSR_ERROR_20261004") } var _ = skgo.Load(errorLoad) ``` 3. Add `web/src/routes/error/+page.svelte` containing `

DEV_DIAG_ERROR_ROUTE_MUST_NOT_RENDER_20261004

`. 4. Add a second `/panic` page with the same registration pattern and a load body of `panic("DEV_DIAG_SSR_PANIC_20261004")`. 5. Run `just dev`, request `/error` and `/panic` through the Go origin, then request a healthy route. Observed in two complete native runs: - Both failed routes return HTTP 500. The rendered error is `

500

Internal Error

`; the hydration error is also `Internal Error`. Neither authored error literal nor user frame is exposed in the development response. - The panic is logged to the terminal with its authored literal, but its frame refers to generated `internal/skgo/links/.../page.server.go`, rather than the authored route path. The returned-error terminal slice contains no authored error/message frame. - The following healthy request returns HTTP 200 with its literal receipt, through the same supervisor and application identities. Expected development behavior: a useful diagnostic with the authored Go error message and an authored route source frame, while preserving ordinary recovery. This request concerns development diagnostics; it does not ask for production error disclosure. Qualification identity: released CLI has exact command/module/version and clean VCS metadata; SHA256 `98645ccab5733e0c7c0f06646dd22c9a59b621c6623576256c64cc28dad8da87`. The actual `go tool skgo dev` runtime and application metadata independently resolved core v0.16.3. No diagnostic logger, backend replacement or injected loader was used. The literals above are synthetic reproduction data.

**Triage — 2026-10-18**

Checked against current [`main` at `920b6aca`](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/tree/920b6aca738a65d6c046a67f4db2373596fafd03). Classification: `bounded-hard`. 

The old goja development stack is gone, but a similar diagnostic gap can still exist in the native bridge. Current dev_bridge.go calls nativeErrorFor, whose tracing_native.go implementation returns no native diagnostic when tracing is disabled and carries kind/message/status without an authored Go source frame. Keep open for a current real-session returned-error/panic reproduction and useful authored diagnostics with recovery. The v0.16.3 response is historical evidence, not a newly reproduced failure.
